campus: Catania — Department of Civil Engineering and Architecture (DICAR), University Campus, Via Santa Sofia 64
admission_type: Open access with verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation. For the general 2026/27 open-access route, the committee first reviews the curriculum and may require an individual interview; non-EU applicants residing abroad follow a public selection based on qualifications with a possible online interview or test.
admission_route: Non-EU citizens residing abroad: non_eu_public_selection_call through the UNICT Student Portal, followed by Universitaly pre-enrolment for the visa. EU/equated citizens and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy: eu_pre_evaluation_webform when the qualifying degree is foreign, followed by the 2026/27 open-access master's admission application in Smart_Edu.
citizenship_track: non_eu_resident_abroad / eu_and_equated / non_eu_resident_in_italy. EU-equated treatment includes the categories specified by UNICT, including citizens of Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and San Marino and qualifying non-EU residents in Italy.
academic_requirements: A bachelor's or higher degree (or a university diploma of at least three years / at least 180 ECTS) in Civil Engineering, Building or Architectural Engineering, or Industrial Engineering. Another Italian or foreign degree may be accepted if the Degree Programme Board considers it suitable. Applicants must have adequate personal preparation and knowledge of the programme's core subjects. For the 2026/27 non-EU-abroad call, a foreign bachelor's or higher degree must follow at least three years of study and permit entry to master's-level study in the country where it was awarded.
eligible_bachelor_backgrounds: Primarily Civil Engineering, Building/Architectural Engineering, and Industrial Engineering. The programme regulations identify Italian degree classes L-7 Civil Engineering and L-9 Industrial Engineering; other degrees, including foreign degrees, may be accepted if deemed suitable by the Degree Programme Board.
curricular_subject_prerequisites: Adequate knowledge of drawing, construction science, environmental and sanitary engineering, materials technology, building construction, building physics and building energy systems, transportation engineering, geotechnics, and hydraulics.
degree_recency_limit: No fixed degree-age exclusion is stated. The 2026/27 general open-access annex says curriculum review remains subject to the University regulation on assessing whether knowledge attached to credits earned more than six years ago is still current.
undergraduate_in_progress_allowed: Yes. Under the 2026/27 non-EU-abroad call, applicants must obtain the bachelor's degree by 31 July 2026. Under the general open-access procedure, graduating students may apply conditionally and may enrol conditionally if, on 1 October 2026, no more than 30 ECTS including the final examination remain; they must graduate by 28 February 2027 to regularize enrolment.
professional_experience_alternative: Candidates seconded from international organisations or national foreign services may also be considered if they hold a university degree and have relevant professional experience. The call does not state that experience can replace the university-degree requirement.
language_requirements: Good written and spoken English at CEFR B2 level or higher. The 2026/27 non-EU-abroad selection requires an accepted certificate or exemption evidence. In the general open-access route, English at no less than B2 may also be assessed during the individual interview.

english_certificate_thresholds.cambridge_min: Cambridge First Certificate in English (FCE) or higher

english_certificate_exemptions: A declaration from the university that awarded the bachelor's or master's degree stating that English was the official language of the programme, or a self-declaration of citizenship of an English-speaking country.
italian_language_requirement: No Italian-language requirement is stated for admission to this English-taught master's programme; the 2026/27 non-EU call page explicitly states that an Italian-language test is not required.
application_deadline_eu: For EU/equated applicants with a foreign qualification, the pre-evaluation webform deadline was 30 June 2026 (form open from 8 April 2026). The subsequent general open-access master's application in Smart_Edu ran from 6 July to 2 September 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu: 17 March 2026 at 23:59 GMT+1 for non-EU applicants residing abroad under D.R. 392 (applications opened 10 February 2026 at 12:00 GMT+1). Admitted visa applicants also had to submit Universitaly pre-enrolment by 31 July 2026.
results_publication_date: By 6 May 2026 for the non-EU-abroad selection (the programme ranking was issued 22 April 2026). Under the general open-access route, initial curriculum-review lists were due by 9 September 2026; results after any interview were due by 24 September 2026.
required_documents: Non-EU-abroad public selection: passport personal-data pages; bachelor's degree certificate or enrolment certificate showing expected graduation date; official translation into Italian or English where needed; transcript listing courses, examinations, grades, pass-mark range and preferably GPA; official syllabi on university letterhead or validated with the university stamp; reference letter, preferably from a university lecturer; Europass-format CV in English; English certificate or exemption evidence; statement of purpose in English (maximum 4,000 characters including spaces); signed summary sheet; and any other useful supporting document. EU/equated foreign-degree pre-evaluation: final secondary-school diploma and Declaration of Value or comparability certificate; bachelor's degree and Declaration of Value or comparability and verification; transcript/Diploma Supplement; official syllabi; motivation letter; recommendation letter; and English certificate.
entry_exam_or_test: Non-EU-abroad applicants are ranked out of 100: curriculum up to 50 points, relevance of prior studies and experience up to 40, reference letter up to 5, and statement of purpose up to 5; 50/100 is the suitability threshold, and the board may invite applicants to an online interview and/or test. In the general open-access route, all curricula are reviewed; only applicants whom the committee considers in need of further verification take an individual interview on core subject areas and B2 English, scheduled for 21 September 2026 at 10:00 in classroom P6, Building 3, Via Santa Sofia 64, or by Microsoft Teams.
credential_recognition_documents: Documents not in Italian or English require an official translation. At enrolment, non-EU visa applicants must provide an ENIC/NARIC (CIMEA) statement of comparability and qualification certification or a Declaration of Value, plus passport with study visa, Italian tax code and residence-permit request. EU/equated applicants with foreign degrees must provide a Declaration of Value or CIMEA verification and comparability; the pre-evaluation page also requests corresponding recognition documentation for the secondary-school qualification. Official syllabi must be on university letterhead or validated by the university stamp.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.unict.it/it/corsi-numero-programmato/2026-2027/public-selection-admission-non-eu-students-living-abroad-english (for non-EU students residing abroad, the linked call sets total 2026/27 enrolment charges at EUR 306: EUR 140 regional tax, EUR 16 stamp duty and EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution). The general open-access procedure and current student-contribution rules are linked from https://www.unict.it/it/corsi-numero-non-programmato/2026-2027/procedura-di-ammissione-al-1%C2%B0-anno-corsi-di-laurea-magistrale .
application_fee: EUR 10 per programme application for the 2026/27 non-EU-abroad public selection. The general open-access route does not charge an application fee upfront, but if an additional written test, test or interview is required, EUR 35 is automatically charged with the second tuition instalment.
enrolment_confirmation_fee: For the non-EU-abroad selection, EUR 75, non-refundable, due within 15 days of the admission notification (the general timeline stated 21 May 2026); it is credited toward the EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution. Under the general open-access route, enrolled students pay a fixed EUR 156 charge comprising the EUR 140 regional tax and EUR 16 stamp duty.
places_quota_non_eu: [uncertain] No numerical non-EU quota is shown in the 2026/27 public-selection course table; its available-places cell is blank.
places_quota_total: [uncertain] No total capacity is published. The official 2026/27 programme page and admission annex classify the course as open/non-restricted access.
application_portal_url: Non-EU abroad and general open-access application: https://studenti.smartedu.unict.it/ ; EU/equated foreign-degree pre-evaluation: https://webform.unict.it/en/pre-evaluation-form-english-taught-master-degree-courses-eu-and-equated-citizens-only ; visa pre-enrolment: https://www.universitaly.it/
governing_decree_reference: Non-EU-abroad selection: D.R. 392 of 4 February 2026. General 2026/27 open-access master's procedure: D.R. 2233 of 23 June 2026. Construction Management and Safety non-EU ranking: D.R. 1448 of 22 April 2026.

source_quotes.quote: Successful applicants come primarily from an academic background in: a. civil engineering; b. building/architectural engineering; c. industrial engineering
IELTS: overall score 5.5 or higher; TOEFL: minimum total score 72
La domanda di ammissione può essere effettuata dal 6 luglio al 2 settembre 2026.
il colloquio potrà svolgersi tramite videoconferenza sulla piattaforma Microsoft Teams

uncertainty_notes: The two 2026/27 routes use different selection mechanics and dates: the early public selection is specifically for non-EU students residing abroad, while the later open-access procedure covers Italian, EU/equated and other eligible applicants. The programme's 2025/26 English academic regulations describe an individual interview for personal preparation, whereas the 2026/27 general annex clarifies that the interview is required only when the committee considers further verification necessary after curriculum review. No published seat quota was found. The EUR 306 tuition figure is specific to non-EU students residing abroad; fees for EU/Italian-equivalent applicants follow the general contribution rules and may vary.
